grammar.title: 教 + somebody + (doing something)
grammar.explanation: 教 takes two objects: first the person being taught, then what they are taught. The thing taught is usually a whole verb phrase (唱歌, 畫畫, 做菜). The subject is the one who knows and gives the knowledge, so 教 always looks at things from the teacher's side.
grammar.contrast: 跟 + person + 學 + Verb Phrase means the opposite direction: 老師教我畫畫 (teacher teaches me) vs 我跟老師學畫畫 (I learn from the teacher). Ask who has the knowledge — that person is the subject of 教, but comes after 跟 with 學.
grammar.common_error: Learners add 給 or reverse the order, saying 他教給我畫畫 or 他教畫畫我. 教 needs no 給, and the person must come right after 教: 他教我畫畫.

examples.gloss: The teacher teaches us to draw.

passage.title: 學校的表演
passage.hanzi: 週末晚上，我跟朋友去學校看表演。第一個節目是唱歌，第二個是跳舞，最後是音樂表演，真的很好聽。我姐姐在學校教小朋友畫畫，她也帶學生來看。我照了很多照片，回家給爸爸媽媽看。他們說下次也要跟我們一起去。
passage.gloss: On the weekend evening, I went with a friend to school to watch a performance. The first item on the program was singing, the second was dancing, and the last was a music performance — it really sounded great. My older sister teaches children painting at the school, and she brought her students to watch too. I took a lot of photos and showed them to my parents when I got home. They said that next time they want to come with us too.

grammar.title: 根據 + source,+ statement (according to …)
grammar.pattern: 根據 + 來源(新聞/歷史書/老師說的),+ 句子
grammar.explanation: 根據 introduces where your information comes from. It goes at the front of the sentence, is followed by a noun or a noun-like phrase (新聞、歷史書、他說的話), and then a comma and the main statement. It is neutral and slightly formal, so it is very common in news, reports and school work.
grammar.contrast: 聽說 ("I hear that…") also starts a sentence, but 聽說 is hearsay with no named source and is followed directly by a clause: 聽說明天有颱風。With 根據 you must name the source: 根據新聞,明天有颱風。If you can point at the source, use 根據; if you only heard it somewhere, use 聽說.
grammar.common_error: Learners use 根據 to mean "in my opinion" and say 根據我,這個很難. 根據 needs an information source, not a person's feelings — say 我覺得這個很難 instead. Also don't put a full clause right after 根據 (not 根據明天下雨…).

passage.title: 老房子的故事
passage.hanzi: 上個週末,我跟爸爸去了台中。那裡有很多老房子,每一間都有自己的故事。爸爸說,根據歷史書,這些房子有一百多年了。這幾十年,城市的變化很大,可是老房子還在。回家以後,我又在新聞上看到那個地方,心裡很高興。
passage.gloss: Last weekend I went to Taichung with my dad. There are many old houses there, and every one of them has its own story. Dad said that according to the history books, these houses are over a hundred years old. Over the past few decades the city has changed a lot, but the old houses are still there. After I got home, I saw that place in the news again, and it made me happy.

grammar.title: Giving good wishes with 祝
grammar.pattern: 祝 + 人 + 好事（快樂／平安／身體健康）
grammar.explanation: 祝 introduces a blessing you are giving someone. Put the person right after 祝, then a short fixed phrase for the good thing you wish them: 祝你生日快樂, 祝你們天天快樂, 祝你一路平安. 祝 is used in speech at weddings and birthdays, and in cards and messages. You do not need 很 or 是 inside the wish, and you never need 了 — 祝 is about the future, not a finished action.
grammar.contrast: 希望 also expresses a wish, but 希望 takes a full clause and can be about yourself: 我希望明天不下雨 / 我希望我能去. 祝 must be aimed at another person plus a set blessing phrase — you cannot say 我祝我考試好. If the wish is your own hope, use 希望; if you are congratulating or blessing someone, use 祝.
grammar.common_error: Learners add 很 or 是 into the blessing (✗祝你很快樂) or attach a whole clause (✗祝你可以結婚). The wish after 祝 stays a short fixed phrase: 祝你快樂, 祝你們結婚快樂.

examples.hanzi: 他們結婚了，我們祝他們天天快樂。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen jiéhūn le, wǒmen zhù tāmen tiāntiān kuàilè.

passage.title: 張老師結婚了
passage.hanzi: 上個週末，張老師在台北的一家飯店舉行結婚餐會。他和他的妻子都還很年輕，兩個人是在大學的舞會上認識的。那天，我們班的同學都去了，還一起送了一個大紅包。我們跟他們說：祝你們天天快樂，身體健康。張老師笑著說，謝謝大家這麼關心他。
passage.gloss: Last weekend Teacher Zhang held his wedding banquet at a hotel in Taipei. He and his wife are both still quite young; the two of them met at a university dance. That day, all the classmates in our class went, and together we gave them a big red envelope. We said to them: we wish you happiness every day and good health. Teacher Zhang smiled and said thank you all for caring about him so much.
